data: The white US spacewalk suit that has flown every American EVA from the Shuttle through the ISS

Modular EVA suit with a hard upper torso, soft fabric arms and legs, and a backpack-mounted Primary Life Support System. Operates at 4.3 psi pure O₂. Originally fielded for Shuttle EVAs (1981), still in service on the ISS. SAFER mini-thruster pack added for tether-loss rescue.
The white US spacewalk suit — every American EVA from the Shuttle to the ISS

Extravehicular Mobility Unit — modular EVA suit with a hard upper torso, soft fabric arms and legs, and a Primary Life Support System backpack. Operates at 4.3 psi pure O₂. First EVA flown on STS-6 (April 1983) and still in service on the ISS more than 40 years later. SAFER mini-thruster pack added in 1994 for tether-loss rescue (1.4 kg N₂, ~3 m/s Δv).
The orange Shuttle pressure suit worn after Challenger made shirtsleeve ascent unacceptable
The J-mission suit — added a waist joint so astronauts could sit in the Lunar Rover
The first operational lunar surface suit — Apollo 11 through 14
The Soyuz launch-entry suit, mandatory since the 1971 Soyuz 11 decompression deaths
China's launch-entry suit, worn on every Shenzhou flight since 2003
